entries.value:
The main gathering I've attended is the Junior Science and Humanities Symposium, where I was a national finalist for my independent research on Valley Fever and environmental disease modeling. I presented the SIR-style epidemiological model I built in Python and the microcontroller-based dust sensor I programmed in C/C++, and most of the value came from talking with other students and researchers about how they were connecting environmental data to health outcomes.

Outside of that, my participation has been through programs rather than conferences: ClarityAtlas, the iOS health product I lead technically, was selected for the Johns Hopkins Pava Spark Accelerator and NSF I-Corps, both of which involved cohort sessions and customer-discovery work with other early-stage teams.

I don't have a confirmed conference schedule for this year yet. I'd be most likely to attend events focused on applied machine learning, LLM evaluation and reliability, or early-stage product building, since that's where most of my work sits, and I'm happy to flag anything I commit to.
